parts.title: My Saturdays at the care home
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When I was thirteen, my mother suggested that I should do some volunteer work. I was not keen. I imagined myself doing boring jobs for people who would not even say thank you. However, my mother had already phoned the local care home, and the next Saturday I was standing in front of the door with a bunch of flowers I had bought, because I did not know what else to bring.

The manager, a cheerful woman called Mrs Adeyemi, took me to the lounge, where about ten residents were drinking tea. She asked me to talk to Mr Bellamy, who sat alone by the window. I was nervous, and my first question was stupid: I asked him if he was bored. He looked at me for a moment, and then he laughed. He told me that he had been a ship's cook for thirty years and had visited forty countries.

After that, I went every Saturday. Mr Bellamy taught me to make a perfect omelette, and in return, I taught him to send photos on his phone. One day, his niece wrote to him from Canada, and he was so happy that he showed the message to everyone in the room.

Last month, Mr Bellamy died, at the age of ninety-one. His family asked me to speak at the funeral, and I said that he had taught me more than any teacher. I am now training to help at a hospital, because I have learnt that listening to people is also a kind of help.

questions.prompt: How did the writer feel about volunteering at first?
questions.explanation: She says she was not keen and imagined boring jobs.

questions.prompt: Why did the writer's first question surprise Mr Bellamy?
options: Nobody had talked to him for a week.
It was not a very polite question.
He was not used to being asked anything.
He had expected a longer speech.
questions.explanation: She asked him if he was bored, which was a stupid question; he looked at her and then laughed.

questions.prompt: What did the writer learn from Mr Bellamy?
options: How to cook a simple dish
questions.explanation: He taught her to make a perfect omelette.

questions.prompt: Why was Mr Bellamy happy one day?
options: He received a message from a relative.
He had a visit from a friend.
He won a prize at the home.
His family came to see him.
questions.explanation: His niece wrote to him from Canada and he showed the message to everyone.

questions.prompt: What is the writer doing now?
options: Writing a book about Mr Bellamy
Preparing to help in a hospital
questions.explanation: She is training to help at a hospital because she has learnt that listening is a kind of help.

parts.title: A moustache for charity
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Every November, thousands of people in the UK take part in a charity challenge called Movember. [1] The name comes from "moustache" and "November", and the aim is to raise money for men's health.

The idea began in Australia about twenty years ago, when two friends decided to grow moustaches for a month. [2] They wanted to start a conversation about health problems that men often do not like to discuss.

Today, the challenge is one of the largest in the world. [3] Women can also take part by supporting the men in their lives, or by walking or running every day. Many companies encourage their staff to join in.

The money pays for research and for services such as telephone helplines. [4] Some of the people who call say that the helpline saved their lives.

For those who take part, it is also a chance to have fun. People send photos of their moustaches to friends, and offices play games. [5] As one volunteer says, "It started as a joke, but it became something serious."
sentences: Men start the month with a clean face and let their moustaches grow for thirty days.
A moustache can look very different on every face.
The first moustache was grown by a man named Fred in 1954.
The helplines are open all day and night, and anybody can call.
However, the competition also makes people think about serious problems.
They got a lot of attention, and people wanted to know why.
Millions of pounds have been raised since it began.
Doctors also advise men to visit them once a year.

gaps.explanation: "Movember" is introduced and then explained: men grow moustaches for thirty days; the next sentence explains the name.
The two friends grew moustaches; they got attention and people wanted to know why, so they wanted to start a conversation.
"One of the largest in the world" is supported by the fact that millions of pounds have been raised; the next sentence adds that women can join too.
The money pays for services such as helplines; the next sentence refers to the helplines being open day and night, and the callers.
"However" links the fun of competitions with the serious side; the volunteer's comment continues the contrast.

parts.title: Short conversations
parts.instructions: Listen to seven short conversations. Choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: aurelio
turns.text: Hi Benedikta, it’s Aurelio. I’m calling about the volunteers’ meeting tomorrow. I know we planned it for nine, and then I sent a message to say ten o’clock because of the bus times. Please forget both. The director’s train from London is delayed, and she doesn’t want to start without her, so the meeting is now at eleven, in the same room as always. There will be coffee and biscuits, and you can still bring your ideas for the spring fair. See you tomorrow, and thanks for being so flexible.

question.prompt: What time is the meeting now?
question.explanation: The meeting was planned for nine, then ten, but the director’s train is late, so it is now at eleven.

turns.speaker: cornelia
turns.text: Desmond, I’m so excited about the beach clean on Saturday. What do I need to bring?

turns.speaker: desmond
turns.text: The council gives us sacks, so there’s no need for bags. And we’ll have lunch at the café after, so I wouldn’t bring a picnic either.

turns.speaker: cornelia
turns.text: What about my hands? Last time I got a cut from a broken bottle.

turns.speaker: desmond
turns.text: That’s the most important thing. Bring your thick gardening ones, or buy some in the shop on the corner. They cost two pounds.

turns.speaker: cornelia
turns.text: Good plan. I’ll get them tomorrow.

turns.speaker: desmond
turns.text: Great. Don’t forget a hat if it’s sunny.

question.prompt: What does the woman need to take?
question.explanation: The council gives the sacks and lunch is at the café, so she only needs gardening gloves to protect her hands from broken glass.

turns.speaker: ernesto
turns.text: Frederika, I’ve added up the money from the cake sale and the raffle. We raised three hundred and forty pounds.

turns.speaker: frederika
turns.text: That’s wonderful! We hoped for three hundred, but I didn’t think we’d get so much.

turns.speaker: ernesto
turns.text: Last year’s total was four hundred and thirty, don’t forget, but that was a bigger event, with a concert.

turns.speaker: frederika
turns.text: Still, this is a good result for a small school. Shall we tell the headteacher?

turns.speaker: ernesto
turns.text: Yes, let’s put it in the newsletter. I’ll write a short article tonight.

turns.speaker: frederika
turns.text: Perfect. Please thank everyone who baked.

question.prompt: How much money did they raise?
question.explanation: They hoped for three hundred and last year they got four hundred and thirty, but this year the total is three hundred and forty.

turns.speaker: gustavo
turns.text: Hildegarde, where shall we meet on Sunday morning for the litter pick? I was thinking of the café, because it opens early.

turns.speaker: hildegarde
turns.text: It’ll be packed with tourists, and we won’t find each other. What about the car park?

turns.speaker: gustavo
turns.text: Not that one. It’s closed this weekend for repairs. And the worst rubbish is at the other end, anyway, past the rocks.

turns.speaker: hildegarde
turns.text: Then let’s meet at the north end of the beach, by the big flag. It’s quiet and we can start straight away.

turns.speaker: gustavo
turns.text: Brilliant. I’ll bring the sacks.

options: At the north end of the beach
question.explanation: The café will be crowded and the car park is closed, so they will meet at the quiet north end where the worst rubbish is.

turns.speaker: isadora
turns.text: Dear parents and students, thank you for coming to our winter fair. I have good news about the money. When we planned the day, we talked about helping the elderly people in the village, and the teachers suggested the children’s ward at the hospital. In the end, the students voted, and they chose something different. All the money will go to the animal shelter on Pine Road, to buy food and blankets for the dogs that wait there for a new home. Thank you for your kindness, and have a lovely evening.

question.prompt: Who will the school's money help?
question.explanation: The older people and the sick children were ideas, but the students voted for the shelter, so the dogs will receive the money.

turns.speaker: kasper
turns.text: Hello, volunteers. This is Kasper with the travel plan for Saturday’s tree planting. We’ll meet at the school at eight. Some of you suggested taking the public bus, but it only runs every two hours and we’d be late. A few people wanted to cycle, because it’s good exercise, but the road to the forest is steep and dangerous. So I’ve hired a minibus from the sports club. It takes fifteen people and leaves at eight fifteen sharp. Please bring your boots and a coat, and we’ll be home by four.

question.explanation: The public bus is too slow and the road is dangerous for cyclists, so he has hired a minibus from the sports club.

turns.speaker: marcellus
turns.text: Nerissa, my nephew wants to volunteer at the charity shop on Saturday. What can he do?

turns.speaker: nerissa
turns.text: Well, we have the tea table, but the older ladies like to do that. Cleaning the floor is another job, though he did that last time, and he found it boring.

turns.speaker: marcellus
turns.text: He’s strong and likes things organised.

turns.speaker: nerissa
turns.text: Then the best job is the back room. People bring us clothes and toys, and we need someone to put them in boxes and stick on the labels for the post. He can do that all day.

turns.speaker: marcellus
turns.text: He’ll love it. Thanks, Nerissa.

question.prompt: What will the boy mainly do?
question.explanation: Tea is done by the older ladies and he found the floor boring; because he is strong and organised, he will put things in boxes and label them for the post.

parts.title: Understanding the main idea
parts.instructions: Listen to six short conversations and choose the best answer.

turns.speaker: octavian
turns.text: Petronella, the hospital asked me to help in the library, but I’m not sure.

turns.speaker: petra2
turns.text: Why not? You love books.

turns.speaker: octavian
turns.text: I’m afraid it’s not for me. I’d like a job with a salary, and it’s every Saturday. I can’t ask for money, they said no.

turns.speaker: petra2
turns.text: I don’t think you should look for something else. Go on a Saturday, see how it feels. If you hate it, you can leave after a month.

turns.speaker: octavian
turns.text: That’s true. There’s nothing to lose.

turns.speaker: petra2
turns.text: Exactly. I’ll bet you enjoy it, and the other volunteers are lovely.

question.prompt: What does the woman encourage the man to do?
question.explanation: He is not sure and cannot be paid, but she says to go once, see how it feels and leave if he hates it.

turns.speaker: quirina
turns.text: Good morning, Seaview Hotel, how can I help?

turns.speaker: raphael
turns.text: Hello. I booked a room for the charity weekend, for Friday and Saturday. I’m calling because I can’t arrive on Friday after all. My train has been cancelled.

turns.speaker: quirina
turns.text: I’m sorry to hear that. Was there a problem with the room?

turns.speaker: raphael
turns.text: No, it’s all perfect, the room and the staff. I found the hotel easily, I’ve been before. I’d like to book for Saturday and Sunday instead.

turns.speaker: quirina
turns.text: I can do that. Let me change it for you. Would you like breakfast on both mornings?

turns.speaker: raphael
turns.text: Yes, please, it’s included, isn’t it?

question.explanation: He has no complaint and knows the way; the train is cancelled, so he wants to move his booking to Saturday and Sunday.

turns.speaker: sylvester
turns.text: Tabea, how’s the book collection going for the school sale?

turns.speaker: tabea
turns.text: Great. We have two boxes already. People are very generous.

turns.speaker: sylvester
turns.text: Good, but please remind everybody that we can’t use books with missing pages or torn covers. Last year we had a lot of old ones, and nobody bought them.

turns.speaker: tabea
turns.text: Right. We don’t have to buy new ones, do we?

turns.speaker: sylvester
turns.text: No, that’s not the idea. We want things that people can enjoy. Clean books, with all the pages.

turns.speaker: tabea
turns.text: I’ll put up a notice today, with a picture of a clean one.

question.prompt: What does the man want people to do with their books?
options: Buy new ones for the sale
question.explanation: He is not asking for new books to be bought; he says that damaged ones do not sell, so he wants clean books with all the pages.

turns.speaker: ulysses
turns.text: Valentina, you look tired. How was your day in the town centre?

turns.speaker: valentina
turns.text: My feet hurt, my voice is almost gone, and I stood for six hours. I’m exhausted!

turns.speaker: ulysses
turns.text: Was it boring? Were people unkind?

turns.speaker: valentina
turns.text: Not at all. Most people were friendly. A man gave me twenty pounds and an old lady gave me her whole purse of coins. We raised more than last year. I’m really glad I did it.

turns.speaker: ulysses
turns.text: Well done. You deserve a hot chocolate, and a long bath with your feet up.

question.prompt: How does the girl feel about collecting money?
question.explanation: She is tired from standing for six hours, but people were friendly and they raised more than last year, so she feels glad.

turns.speaker: winifred2
turns.text: Xavier, some people say the volunteers at the hospital should get a salary.

turns.speaker: xavier
turns.text: It might be fair. They work hard, sometimes eight hours a day.

turns.speaker: winifred2
turns.text: But then it wouldn’t be volunteering. The whole point is that you give your time for nothing, because you care. If you paid people, the charity would have less money for patients.

turns.speaker: xavier
turns.text: I see. Maybe a lunch or a bus ticket?

turns.speaker: winifred2
turns.text: Yes, that would be okay. But I think the hours are a personal choice. I enjoy mine, so I wouldn’t change anything.

options: Volunteers should give their time free.
Volunteers should work for fewer hours.
question.explanation: Paying would stop it from being volunteering and the charity would have less money, so she thinks people should give their time for nothing.

turns.speaker: yolanda
turns.text: Zacharias, hi! It’s Yolanda from the charity shop. How are you?

turns.speaker: zacharias
turns.text: Hello, Yolanda. I’m fine, thanks. Is everything okay?

turns.speaker: yolanda
turns.text: Everything’s fine, but we miss you on Saturdays. Since you left in September, the shelves have been so untidy. Nobody organises the books like you do.

turns.speaker: zacharias
turns.text: That’s kind. I stopped because of my exams, but they finish next week.

turns.speaker: yolanda
turns.text: Then could you come back at the end of the month? We would be really happy.

turns.speaker: zacharias
turns.text: Of course, I’d love to. I’ll bring some books from home, too.

options: Asking a helper to come back
question.explanation: She says they miss him since September and asks if he can come back at the end of the month.

parts.title: A talk about a charity run
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: speaker-1
turns.text: Hello, everyone, and thank you for coming. I’m Dorothea, and I’m organising this year’s Fun Run for the children’s hospital. Let me give you the details. The run will take place on Sunday. Last year it was held on a Saturday, but a lot of families couldn’t come because of football matches, so we moved it. We expect about three hundred runners. There are two routes, a long one of ten kilometres for serious runners, and a shorter one of five kilometres for families, and most people choose this one. It’s flat, and children can walk if they get tired. The start is in Millford Park. Some people believe it begins in Millford Square, because that’s where the finish line was last time, but this year everything is in the park, by the big fountain. There’s a cafe, toilets and plenty of space for the pushchairs. At the start, every runner will get a T-shirt. Last year they were blue, but we have changed the colour to yellow, which is more cheerful, and the children’s hospital will be on the front. Please wear it on the day, so that we can see you from far away. Now, how do you sign up? You can call the office on weekdays, but the line is always busy, so it’s much quicker to register on our website. It takes about two minutes, and you pay by card. The entry fee for adults is ten pounds, and children run for free. Finally, why are we doing this? The hospital has a small waiting room for the young patients. With the money, we plan to buy toys and books for it. Last year we bought a television, but the children told us they would prefer something to read. Thank you for listening, and I hope to see you all there!

gaps.prompt: The charity run is held on a ___ this year
gaps.explanation: They moved it from Saturday to Sunday.

gaps.prompt: The shorter route, which most families choose, is ___ kilometres long
gaps.explanation: The long route is ten kilometres; most people choose the five-kilometre one.

gaps.prompt: Everybody gathers in Millford ___ by the fountain
gaps.explanation: It is not the square; everything is in the park.

gaps.prompt: Each runner will receive a ___ shirt with the hospital's name
gaps.explanation: Last year’s shirts were blue; this year they are yellow.

gaps.prompt: The quickest way to sign up is on the charity's ___
gaps.explanation: The phone line is always busy; the quickest way is the website.

gaps.prompt: The hospital's waiting room will get toys and ___
gaps.explanation: Last year they bought a television; this time the children prefer something to read, so books.

parts.title: An interview with a soup kitchen manager
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Cuthbert, you run a soup kitchen in the city centre. How did it start?

turns.speaker: barnaby3
turns.text: Fifteen years ago, I was a chef in a hotel. One winter night, I saw a hungry man in the street, looking for food in a bin. That shocked me. A hotel manager did ask me about helping once, but that was later, and I have never seen the programme about it on television. It was that man, that night. The next day I started to take the leftovers to the people who slept near the station. I had no plan, only a few big pots and a lot of worry. Within a month, thirty people were waiting for me every night.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Who works in the kitchen today?

turns.speaker: barnaby3
turns.text: Not just trained chefs, though two of my old friends from the hotel still come. We have forty volunteers. Some of them are students, some are retired, and a few are people who used to eat here and now want to give something back. I’m very proud of that, and it makes the room feel like a family. They understand the customers better than anybody.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Where does the food come from?

turns.speaker: barnaby3
turns.text: Mostly from supermarkets, which give us fruit and vegetables that are slightly damaged but perfectly good. Farmers bring potatoes at harvest time, but that’s only for a few weeks. Hotels sometimes send us bread, but not regularly, because they plan carefully and waste little.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Is winter different?

turns.speaker: barnaby3
turns.text: There’s no more food then, in fact there’s less, because people buy more for Christmas. And the number of customers doesn’t drop either. The cold is the problem. The queue grows longer, and standing outside for an hour is hard for people. We are trying to find a bigger building with a waiting room, but the rents in this part of the city are very high, so it may take a long time.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would you like people to understand?

turns.speaker: barnaby3
turns.text: That anybody can end up in difficulty. A job loss, an illness, a family problem, and everything can change very quickly. Some think that our customers don’t want to work, but that isn’t true, many have jobs. And we help everyone, whether they live here or not. The people who come here are not different from you or me. I really want everyone to remember that.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How can people help?

turns.speaker: barnaby3
turns.text: Old clothes are welcome, but we send them to another charity. Money helps, of course, but time is even more valuable. Even two hours a month makes a difference. And a smile and a kind word cost nothing.

questions.prompt: What made Cuthbert start the kitchen?
options: A request from a hotel manager
Seeing a hungry man in the street
questions.explanation: The hotel manager came later and he never saw the programme; it was the hungry man looking in a bin that shocked him.

questions.prompt: Who works in the kitchen?
questions.explanation: Two old friends are chefs, but most of the forty volunteers are students and retired people, and some used to eat there.

questions.prompt: Where does most of the food come from?
questions.explanation: Farmers only bring potatoes for a few weeks and hotels send bread rarely; most of the food is from supermarkets.

questions.prompt: What does he say about the winter?
options: People queue outside in the cold.
questions.explanation: There is less food and the same number of customers; the problem is the long queue in the cold.

questions.prompt: What does he want people to understand?
options: Most customers do not want to work.
Anyone can end up needing help.
The service is only for local people.
questions.explanation: Customers do want to work and the help is for everyone; he wants people to know that anybody can end up in difficulty.

questions.prompt: What does he say is most useful for volunteers to give?
questions.explanation: Clothes go to another charity and money helps, but time is even more valuable.

parts.title: Getting to know you
parts.instructions: Answer each question in your own words. Aim to speak for 20-30 seconds.

questions.prompt: Have you ever helped other people? What did you do?
Which charities or causes do you think are important? Why?
Tell me about someone you know who does volunteer work.
Would you like to be a volunteer in the future? Why, or why not?
